name: Ependymal Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Histological identification of ependymal rosettes or perivascular pseudorosettes
MRI showing well-demarcated intraventricular or spinal cord mass with heterogeneous enhancement
Positive staining for GFAP and EMA with dot-like pattern
Detection of RELA fusion or other molecular alterations in specific subtypes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic imaging and immunohistochemical findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing aids in subclassification and prognosis but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to obstructive intraventricular mass
pathognomonic.notes: Common in intracranial ependymomas causing increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain from blocked ventricle
brain swelling due to mass blocking fluid
tumor cells arranged around blood vessels
ring of cells around vessels in biopsy

common.symptomName: Headache secondary to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain due to raised intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to spinal cord involvement
searchTerms: walking problems from spinal cord damage
difficulty walking due to spine issues

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to increased intracranial pressure
Sensory deficits in affected spinal segments
searchTerms: loss of sensation in spinal nerve areas
bladder control problems from spinal tumor
urinary dysfunction due to spine tumor

occasional.symptomName: Diplopia due to cranial nerve involvement

searchTerms: loss of coordination from cerebellar pressure
balance problems due to brain compression
memory and thinking decline from tumors
cognitive problems with long-term brain tumors
mental decline due to tumor growth

laboratory: CSF cytology may show tumor cells in disseminated disease
Elevated CSF protein in some cases
imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed intraventricular or spinal cord mass
genetic: RELA fusion gene in supratentorial ependymomas
Chromosome 1q gain associated with poor prognosis
other: Histopathology demonstrating ependymal rosettes and perivascular pseudorosettes
Immunohistochemistry positive for GFAP and EMA

distinguishingFeatures: Different immunohistochemical profile (GFAP positive but EMA negative)
Arises from choroid plexus rather than ependymal lining

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure (papilledema, severe headache, vomiting)
New onset seizures in a child or young adult
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC, 2021.
Louis DN, et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System: a summary. Neuro Oncol. 2021.
